title: burst-absorber-fabric-stabilization-and-graceful-quota-failover
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement:
We observed recurring customer-visible capacity failures when regional rate-limiters enter overload or experience transient outages. Symptoms: per-API-key tokens exhausted rapidly during traffic spikes, cross-region retries amplifying bursts, and uniform global failure when the central quota authority becomes unavailable. Current circuit-breakers are too coarse: they either drop everything or allow costly retries. We need a resilient mitigation that: 1) absorbs short-lived hotspots locally without losing fairness, 2) gracefully fails over quotas to adjacent regions when a local limiter is unhealthy, and 3) keeps SLOs for quota-enforcement availability and degradation within acceptable bounds.

Goals and SLOs:
- Quota enforcement availability: 99.95% regional uptime for limiter APIs (control plane) per calendar month.
- Degraded-mode correctness: when a region loses connectivity to the quota authority, requests can still be admitted at a bounded reduced rate such that overall fairness is preserved and downstream latency SLO degradation stays within 2x baseline.
- Failover RTO: automated safe failover to an adjacent region within 30s for routing tier; full traffic rebalancing within 5 minutes.

Scope:
- Implement a local burst-absorber fabric (stateless token-bucket frontends + soft-credit ledger) that can absorb short spikes and reconcile with the global quota service asynchronously.
- Add a hierarchical quota model: immediate local credits + borrowable soft credits from region-adjacent peers with explicit reconciliation windows and debt limits.
- Circuit-breaker policy refinement: progressive throttles with tenant-weighted fairness, adaptive backoff tuned by SLO signals, and explicit degraded-mode admission rules.
- Observability: new SLO dashboards, per-tenant fairness metrics, debt telemetry, and chaos tests for limiter outages.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype: build a proof-of-concept local absorber that accepts bursts for configured keys using in-memory soft credits and emits reconciliation events to the central quota service. (2w)
2) Simulation: run synthetic traffic generator (burst+retry patterns) in a multi-region testbed; measure fairness regressions and tail latencies. (1w)
3) Integrate peer-borrowing: allow neighboring regions to grant short-term soft credits with agreed debt caps. Implement safety checks to avoid double-spend. (2w)
4) Circuit-breaker tuning: implement progressive shed stages (warning, soft-throttle, hard-throttle) driven by token debt and SLO signals; include tenant-weighted eviction. (1w)
5) Observability & runbooks: add dashboards, create incident playbook for limiter outage, and define canary rollout steps. (1w)
6) Rollout: phased canary (5% traffic for 24h, 25% for 48h, full) with automated rollback on SLO regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit/integration tests for absorber reconciliation logic and debt edge cases added.
- End-to-end chaos test with simulated regional quota authority outage shows degraded admission path keeps error rate below 5% and per-tenant fairness deviation within tolerance.
- Dashboard panels for debt, borrow-rate, reconciliation lag, and regional limiter availability created and reviewed by SRE.
- Canary completes without triggering rollback conditions (defined in rollout_plan).
- Design doc and security review notes linked and approved.

Rollout_plan:
- Canary 1 (internal test orgs): 2h smoke -> 24h run -> confirm metrics.
- Canary 2 (low-traffic customers): 48h run with automated SLO checks; monitor debt accumulation.
- Gradual ramp to 100% over 72 hours with pause points and manual review if debt > 20% of allowed cap.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Consistency vs availability: allowing local soft credits introduces temporary divergence between local and global quotas; reconciliation complexity increases.
- Cost: additional compute to hold short-term bursts and cross-region transfer costs for reconciliation events.
- Attack surface: need throttles to prevent abuse where malicious clients intentionally create debt. Mitigation: tenant-weighted caps and anomaly detection.
- Operational complexity: new failure modes (stuck debt, asymmetric borrowing) require observability and automatic eviction heuristics.

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Debt accounting model: precise cost/weight formula for multi-tenant fairness (linear vs exponential penalties).
- Borrow topology: pairwise neighbor vs global staggered fallback.
- Safe debt cap defaults per customer tier.

Chaos scenario for regional quota authority outage demonstrates <5% error rate and acceptable fairness deviation

comments: 2026-02-22 - Arjun Patel: Spiked a simple in-memory absorber prototype. Observed that short 1s bursts were fully absorbed but reconciliation creates debt spikes in the central ledger when bursts are frequent.
2026-02-28 - Priya Nair (SRE): Reviewed prototype metrics. Request adding per-tenant debt caps and prometheus metrics for borrow_rate and reconciliation_lag.
2026-03-03 - Design review (Sophie Laurent): Approved hierarchical quota model conceptually. Asked for clear user-facing behavior doc for degraded mode and tenant expectations.
2026-03-09 - Security (Diego Ramos): Noted vector where borrowers could be used to bypass per-tenant limits via collusion. Recommended rate-limited borrow requests and audit logs; no blocking issues.
2026-03-10 - Arjun Patel: Implemented safe debt cap enforcement and added initial dashboard panels. Starting canary in staging cluster today.
